name: Palao (Odia Style)
instructions: 1. Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes, then drain thoroughly. 2. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker. 3. Add bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom, and sauté until fragrant. 4. Add cashew nuts and raisins, frying until golden. 5. Add the ginger paste and soaked rice, sautéing gently for a few minutes until the grains are coated with ghee. 6. Pour in warm water (double the volume of rice) along with salt and a pinch of sugar. 7. Cover and cook on low heat until the water is absorbed and rice is fluffy. 8. Let it rest for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
description: Odia Palao is a staple celebratory dish in Odisha, often served during festivals, weddings, and special temple offerings (Mahaprasad). Unlike its spicy North Indian counterparts, the Odia version is known for its subtle sweetness, rich aroma of ghee, and the delicate texture of the short-grained Gobindobhog rice.
